claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively homogeneous microstructure lacking secondary nanoscale precipitates.
Vacuum annealing at approximately 700°C for 30–60 minutes followed by controlled cooling will induce nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates in the coating.
The annealing-induced Cu-rich precipitates will be evenly dispersed within the high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates impede dislocation motion in FeNiCrCoCu.
Impedance of dislocation motion by the precipitates produces precipitation hardening.
Precipitation hardening will limit localized plastic flow during sliding.
The precipitates will suppress concentrated deformation zones during high-temperature sliding.
The annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the unannealed baseline coating.
The annealed coating will exhibit more uniform and less localized microscopic deformation than the baseline coating.
The annealed coating will exhibit fewer shear bands or localized plasticity zones than the baseline coating.
The predicted wear and deformation effects should hold during sliding at 600–700°C in vacuum or a controlled inert atmosphere.
Performance may differ outside 600–700°C or in significantly different environments such as oxidizing atmospheres.
The long-term thermal stability of the Cu-rich precipitates near 700°C is uncertain.
The quantitative extent of precipitate-induced dislocation pinning during prolonged high-temperature exposure is uncertain.
